---
title: "Papers and citation"
description: "The preprints behind the packages, and how to cite each one."
---

Two of the three packages have a methods preprint on arXiv. Neither has been
through peer review yet, so cite them as preprints. splitGraph has no paper
yet — cite the package itself.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
Publication status changes. `citation()` in R is the authoritative reference and
is updated on release:

``` r
citation("splitGraph")
citation("bioLeak")
citation("fastml")
```
:::

## fastml

**fastml: Guarded Resampling Workflows for Safer Automated Machine Learning in R**

Selcuk Korkmaz, Dincer Goksuluk, Eda Karaismailoglu.
[arXiv:2604.05225](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05225) \[stat.CO\], 6 April 2026.
Preprint, not peer reviewed.

The argument: AutoML tools compete on model search while leaving the evaluation
design to the user, which is where the errors actually are. Constraining the
workflow so that preprocessing cannot escape the resampling loop removes a whole
class of user-induced error at no statistical cost.

``` bibtex
@misc{korkmaz2026fastml,
  title         = {fastml: Guarded Resampling Workflows for Safer Automated Machine Learning in R},
  author        = {Korkmaz, Selcuk and Goksuluk, Dincer and Karaismailoglu, Eda},
  year          = {2026},
  eprint        = {2604.05225},
  archivePrefix = {arXiv},
  primaryClass  = {stat.CO},
  url           = {https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05225}
}
```

## bioLeak

**bioLeak: Leakage-Aware Modeling and Diagnostics for Machine Learning in R**

Selçuk Korkmaz.
[arXiv:2604.10965](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10965) \[stat.CO\], 13 April 2026.
Preprint, not peer reviewed.

The argument: leakage-aware resampling is necessary but not sufficient. Once
folds are clean you still need evidence about what remains — permutation gaps,
batch association, target-leakage scans — and that evidence should be produced
by the same machinery that produced the estimate.

``` bibtex
@misc{korkmaz2026bioleak,
  title         = {bioLeak: Leakage-Aware Modeling and Diagnostics for Machine Learning in R},
  author        = {Korkmaz, Sel\c{c}uk},
  year          = {2026},
  eprint        = {2604.10965},
  archivePrefix = {arXiv},
  primaryClass  = {stat.CO},
  url           = {https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10965}
}
```

## splitGraph

No preprint yet. Cite the package:

``` r
citation("splitGraph")
```

which currently yields a software citation — author, year, version, and URL. The
manuscript is in preparation; this page will carry it once it is posted.

## Citing the family

There is no paper for the collection, because there is no package for the
collection. Cite the packages you actually used.

If you are describing the overall approach in a methods section, the honest
phrasing is something like:

> Dataset dependency structure was encoded and validated with **splitGraph**
> [ref], leakage-resistant resampling and post-hoc leakage auditing were
> performed with **bioLeak** [ref], and model training and comparison used
> **fastml** [ref] with the resampling scheme fixed upstream.

The last clause matters: it is the part a reader cannot verify from the usual
methods boilerplate, and it is the part that makes the rest meaningful.
